# Intermittent bridge_run_failures during 2026-08-26->28 sweep window

## Impact
The reconcile-bridge recorded **5 isolated single-hour failures** over the sweep window. Each
self-cleared, so no sustained outage, but the pattern is recurring and there is no open ticket
tracking it. Unlike the closed sustained-outage bug eab8 (exceedable-giant-mussel, a pydantic
`SecretStr` import regression fixed 2026-08-18), these are sparse transient failures with a
different signature.

## Evidence — CloudWatch (rebar/host:bridge_run_failures, Sum>0 per hour, PDT)
- 2026-08-26 20:00
- 2026-08-27 15:00
- 2026-08-27 19:00
- 2026-08-27 22:00
- 2026-08-28 01:00

Alarm `rebar-bridge-run-failures` (2-of-2 hourly datapoints > 0) flapped ALARM->OK three times:
- 08-27 19:09 -> 19:47 PDT
- 08-27 22:10 -> 23:09 PDT
- 08-28 01:12 -> 02:10 PDT

## Root-cause status — RESOLVED: env_integration (disk-pressure)
Attributed to ENOSPC during the box-wide disk-fill incident P1 `5a05-0e52-33a0-48bf`
(rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high). All 5 failures fall inside the 5a05 disk-pressure window (alarm
open since 08-26 17:55 unrecovered; root-disk ~18 flaps, peak 98%, 08-26..08-28). Under a full
disk, a state write / store git commit (reconcile child) or `commit-and-push --strict` (delivery
child, `_bridge_runner.py:286`) hard-fails → OPERATIONAL_FAILURE; the next hour, pressure eased,
the pass succeeds — matching the scattered self-clearing signature. No bridge/reconciler code
defect: failing loud under ENOSPC is correct. See the RCA + final comment. Orchestrator accepted
the temporal correlation in lieu of unavailable on-box journald.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] Pull the reconcile-bridge journald/log lines for the 5 timestamps above and
      classify the failure(s).
      provenance: environment=rebar-tracker+CloudWatch-metrics (on-box journald unavailable — the box ships no bridge log group and this session has no on-box access); principal=copilot-cli-reconciler-debug-session; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=static-analysis — the journald pull was not executable from this session, so classification was established by temporally correlating the 5 CloudWatch failure timestamps to the 5a05 disk-fill window (via ledger b2dc), which the orchestrator accepted in lieu of journald.
- [x] Determine whether they are disk-pressure-induced (correlate with the data-disk incident)
      or an independent transient (network/Jira/auth), and fix the class or document as benign.
      — Determined DISK-PRESSURE-INDUCED: all 5 failures fall inside the 5a05 disk-fill window;
      documented as env_integration (benign — no reconciler defect; will not recur once 5a05 is
      remediated). Follow-up fe28-c6d0-b20c-4571 files the optional monitoring-contract enhancement.

## Notes
Filed by a READ-ONLY AWS ops sweep; no AWS mutation performed.
